Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

TEXT_D:
Summary of the Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 (ideological framing preserved)

Core mission
- Stick with the plan that restored stability after Covid and Ukraine: lower inflation, rising real wages, growth returning, and tax cuts. Reward hard work, defend British values, strengthen families and communities, and secure borders, energy and food. The alternative under Labour is higher taxes, unfunded spending, weaker borders and defence.

Tax, work and business
- Halve employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate NI for the self‑employed by the end of the Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT.
- Triple Lock Plus: both State Pension and pensioners’ tax-free allowance rise by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%.
- 30 hours’ free childcare from nine months old; Child Benefit based on household income with support tapering from £120k–£160k.
- Back SMEs with a 10‑point plan; keep corporation tax where it is; extend full expensing when affordable; cut red tape using Brexit freedoms.

Education and opportunity
- Mandatory National Service at 18: competitive paid military/cyber placements or civic service roles.
- 100,000 more high-quality apprenticeships funded by curbing poor‑value degrees.
- Advanced British Standard to end the academic/technical divide; ban phones in school; restore parental rights over what children are taught.

Borders, security and defence
- Legal annual cap on migration that falls each year and is voted on by Parliament.
- Monthly removal flights to Rwanda to stop the boats; rewrite asylum rules with allies; more returns deals.
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; boost munitions, innovation and UK defence industry; unwavering support for Ukraine and Trident.

NHS and welfare
- NHS funding up each year above inflation; 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors; Pharmacy First, new GP surgeries and Community Diagnostic Centres.
- £3.4bn tech upgrade: NHS App as single front door; AI to free clinicians; faster scans; cut 5,500 managers.
- Dental Recovery Plan and new obligations for newly qualified dentists to serve in the NHS.
- Implement the Cass Review: evidence‑based care, protect single‑sex spaces; legislate that “sex” in the Equality Act means biological sex.
- Welfare reform: tighten PIP and work capability assessments; overhaul fit notes; tougher sanctions; accelerate Universal Credit; new Fraud Bill.

Energy, net zero and bills
- Pragmatic, affordable net zero by 2050 with no new green levies or forced rip‑outs. Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing; new gas power stations to back up renewables.
- Treble offshore wind; carbon capture clusters; approve two SMR fleets and deliver Wylfa; speed up grid connections.
- Maintain price cap; PumpWatch for fair fuel prices; household efficiency and solar vouchers.

Homes, communities and crime
- 1.6 million homes: brownfield fast‑track, higher density in cities, scrap EU nutrient rules (with mitigation), new Help to Buy, permanent Stamp Duty relief for first‑time buyers.
- Leasehold reform; fairer private renting with Section 21 abolished after court reforms; CGT relief for landlords selling to sitting tenants.
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; Hotspot Policing; tougher sentences for violent and sexual offenders; Martyn’s Law; crack down on fraud and anti‑social behaviour.

Rural, farming, fishing and drivers
- Legal food security target; farming budget up £1bn and ringfenced; fast‑track farm infrastructure; new Seafood Fund; back inshore fleets.
- Back drivers: no road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for LTNs/20mph; £2 bus fare cap extended.

Union, trade and innovation
- Protect the UK internal market and the Union; level up across Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland; Intertrade UK.
- Lead in AI/R&D; maintain R&D tax reliefs; push new trade deals (India, GCC, CPTPP) without compromising sovereignty or the NHS.

TEXT_C:
Labour Party Manifesto 2024 — Summary (within 500 words)

Framing and purpose
- It’s time for change: end 14 years of Conservative chaos that harmed family finances and public services. Restore hope, turn the page, and rebuild a country that serves working people.
- Mission-driven government: ambitious, measurable national missions delivered with fiscal responsibility, partnership with business and unions, and power pushed out to communities.

Strong foundations
- National security: unshakeable NATO commitment and UK nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review and path to 2.5% of GDP; tougher counter-espionage and counter-extremism; Martyn’s Law.
- Secure borders: create a Border Security Command, end the failing Rwanda scheme, smash smuggler gangs, hire caseworkers to clear the asylum backlog, fast-track returns, and secure a UK–EU security pact.
- Economic stability: strict fiscal rules with independent OBR oversight; no rises in NI, Income Tax rates or VAT; modernise HMRC and close loopholes (non-dom, offshore trusts, carried interest). Keep taxes on working people as low as possible.

Five missions
1) Kickstart growth: pro-business and pro-worker “securonomics”
- Industrial Strategy Council; National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd-in private investment (ports, gigafactories, steel, CCS, green hydrogen).
- Stable business taxes: cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Infrastructure: 10-year plan; faster planning for nationally significant projects; full gigabit and national 5G by 2030.
- Transport: fix roads and 1m extra potholes/year; accelerate EV rollout; bring rail into public ownership as contracts end; empower mayors on integrated transport; bus franchising and lift municipal ownership ban.
- Innovation: 10-year R&D budgets; Regulatory Innovation Office; binding rules for powerful AI models; double co-ops and mutuals; small business late-payment crackdown.
- Housing: 1.5m homes; restore targets; brownfield-first with strategic “grey belt” release; new towns; more social and affordable homes; first-time buyer protections; permanent mortgage guarantee.
- Devolution: Local Growth Plans; multi-year council funding; reform local audit.
- Immigration and skills: reduce net migration with linked skills plans; end long-term shortage list dependence.
- Work and pay: New Deal for Working People—ban exploitative zero-hours contracts, end fire-and-rehire, day-one rights, Single Enforcement Body, genuine living wage without age discrimination. Youth Guarantee (18–21).

2) Make Britain a clean energy superpower by 2030
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co-invest and deploy local power; double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, marine; extend nuclear (Hinkley, Sizewell C, SMRs); strategic gas reserve.
- No new North Sea exploration licences; tougher windfall tax; Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; carbon border adjustment; clean up rivers with tougher enforcement; restore nature; back British farmers; stronger animal welfare.

3) Take back our streets
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; crack down on antisocial behaviour (Respect Orders); new offence for assaults on shopworkers.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory interventions, ban zombie-style blades and online sales abuses; Young Futures hubs nationwide.
- Halve violence against women and girls: specialist RASSO units in every force; fast-track rape courts; stronger stalking, spiking, and policing standards; fix prisons and reduce reoffending; Hillsborough Law.

4) Break down barriers to opportunity
- 3,000 school-based nurseries; free breakfast clubs in every primary school.
- 6,500 new teachers; curriculum and assessment reform; mental health professionals in every school.
- Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; flexible Growth and Skills Levy; secure higher education; broaden access to arts and sport.
- Family security: review Universal Credit to make work pay; end Section 21 evictions; leasehold to commonhold; homelessness strategy; pensions triple lock.

5) Build an NHS fit for the future
- 40,000 extra weekly appointments; shared waiting lists; use independent capacity to cut waits.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; speed innovation and clinical trials.
- Return of the family doctor: more GPs, continuity of care, pharmacist prescribing, Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan (700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform); National Care Service with Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 extra mental health staff; bold public health measures (smoking, youth vaping, junk-food ads).

Clean politics and a reconnected Britain
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; modernise the Commons; immediate Lords reform (end hereditary peers, retirement at 80), path to replacement; votes at 16; reset with devolved governments.
- Foreign policy: strong NATO, support Ukraine, AUKUS, clear-eyed China strategy; make Brexit work with better EU ties (trade, security, vets/MRAs); targeted trade deals (incl. India); lead a Clean Power Alliance; modernise development and restore 0.7% when fiscally possible.

All fully costed and funded within Labour’s fiscal rules. Stop the chaos. Turn the page. Rebuild a Britain that serves working people.

Judge whether A or B aligns more closely with this profile.
